works.title: Helsinki Central Station
works.credit: Helsinki Central Railway Station and Tram (2024).jpg. Sandun De Silva. CC BY-SA 4.0.
works.intro: 埃利爾·薩里寧設計、1919 年落成。花崗岩立面、鐘樓與門口的提燈巨像，是芬蘭民族浪漫主義轉向現代的節點。

works.title: Paimio Sanatorium
works.credit: Paimio Sanatorium2.jpg. Leon Liao from Barcelona, España. CC BY 2.0.
works.intro: 阿爾瓦·阿爾托為結核病療養院做的白色現代主義建築。橫向長窗把休養做成節奏。

works.title: Viipuri Library
works.credit: Alvar Aalto Library Vyborg3.jpg. Ninaraas. CC BY 4.0.
works.intro: 阿爾托在維堡的圖書館。波浪形木天花與圓形天窗把北歐光線做成建築本身。

works.title: Bauhaus Dessau
works.credit: Bauhaus Dessau 2018.jpg. Aufbacksalami. CC BY-SA 4.0.
works.intro: 格羅皮烏斯的德紹校舍。玻璃幕牆與不對稱體量，是二十世紀平面與建築共用的幾何語法。

works.title: Fagus-Werk
works.credit: Fagus-Werk Alfeld 01.jpg. Clemensfranz. CC BY-SA 4.0.
works.intro: 格羅皮烏斯與邁耶的製鞋廠。全玻璃轉角成為後來包豪斯建築的前奏。

works.title: Otaniemi Undergraduate Centre
works.credit: Helsinki University of Technology Main Building, Otaniemi, Espoo (October 2018).jpg. Markus Säynevirta. CC BY-SA 4.0.

works.title: Kulttuuritalo
works.credit: Kulttuuritalo Helsinki.jpg. Mikkoau. CC BY-SA 4.0.
works.intro: 赫爾辛基文化之家。楔形禮堂與紅磚辦公室連成一條街，公共建築的節奏從這裡開始。

works.title: Kela Headquarters
works.credit: Kela hdqtrs 11.JPG. Htm. CC BY-SA 3.0.
works.intro: 國民年金局總部。機構建築的混凝土與紅磚，尺度克制，是芬蘭官僚空間裡少見的安靜。

works.title: Säynätsalo Town Hall
works.credit: Säynatsalo. MaSii. Public domain.
works.intro: 阿爾托的市政廳。紅磚庭院與階梯草坡把行政建築做成一座小聚落。

works.title: Finlandia Hall
works.credit: Finlandia Hall, Helsinki, Finland (2025-01) – 07. Ninara. CC BY 2.0.
works.intro: 阿爾托的芬蘭大廳。卡拉拉白大理石外牆與彎曲木作，把公共廳堂做成一件大型器物。

works.title: Temppeliaukio Church
works.credit: Interior of Temppeliaukio Church, Helsinki, Finland.jpg. Uhooep. CC BY-SA 4.0.
works.intro: 岩石教堂。從巖盤鑿出的圓廳與銅製天花，光線從岩壁與屋頂之間的縫進來。乾淨、沉重、有節奏。

works.title: May Milton
works.credit: May Milton, 1895. Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec (French, 1864–1901). Color lithograph; sheet: 79.5 x 61.5 cm (31 5/16 x 24 3/16 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Mr. and Mrs. Lewis B. Williams Collection, 1952.10
works.intro: Posters grew in popularity after 1881, when many restrictions on their placement were lifted and it became unlawful to remove or destroy them. The first exhibition of posters took place in 1884, and they were soon accepted as a legitimate art form. Lautrec, a gifted draftsman, excelled at designing arresting lithographs. May Milton , one of his boldest compositions, illustrates Lautrec's innovative style based on a dynamic pattern of flat, simplified, brightly colored shapes and dramatic silhouettes. Lautrec, an astute observer of character and physical features, captured the life of a decadent era in his radically concise, vigorous representations. May Milton was an English dancer who appeared at the Moulin Rouge, one of Paris's most popular café-concerts. This poster was made to advertise her tour of the United States.

works.title: Sculptress
works.medium: lithograph with watercolor added by hand
works.credit: Sculptress, 1897. Eugène Grasset (French, 1841–1917). Lithograph with watercolor added by hand; sheet: 64.5 x 49.5 cm (25 3/8 x 19 1/2 in.); image: 53.1 x 37 cm (20 7/8 x 14 9/16 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Henry H. Hawley, 1986.136
works.intro: Grasset, greatly influenced by the art of Japan, Persia, and Egypt, created designs for stained glass windows, furniture, tapestries, and fabrics. This female allegory of Sculpture was meant for an 1898 exhibition poster. Only the black areas and lines were printed. Rather than using a separate stone to print each color, watercolor was applied with the aid of a stencil.

works.title: Poster for the Lembrée Gallery
works.credit: Poster for the Lembrée Gallery, 1897. Theo van Rysselberghe (Belgian, 1862–1926). Color lithograph; image: 62.5 x 44.3 cm (24 5/8 x 17 7/16 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Mr. and Mrs. Charles G. Prasse Collection, 1968.257
works.intro: Poster for the Lembrée Gallery（1897）。克利夫蘭藝術博物館開放典藏。

works.title: Lorenzaccio
works.credit: Lorenzaccio, 1896–1900. Alphonse Mucha (Czech, 1860–1939). Color lithograph; sheet: 39.9 x 29 cm (15 11/16 x 11 7/16 in.); image: 32.6 x 11.2 cm (12 13/16 x 4 7/16 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, The Harold T. Clark Educational Extension Fund, 1973.1018

works.title: Sagot's Gallery
works.medium: color proof of the Remarque Woman with Cat
works.credit: Sagot's Gallery, 1898. Georges Alfred Bottini (French, 1874–1907). Color proof of the Remarque Woman with Cat; sheet: 39.2 x 24 cm (15 7/16 x 9 7/16 in.); image: 10.7 x 6.7 cm (4 3/16 x 2 5/8 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, John L. Severance Fund, 1998.42.7
works.intro: The last decades of the 19th century was the golden era of French color lithography. Jules Cheret (1836–1932) popularized the technique to make colorful posters which, by 1884, were also exhibited as a legitimate art form. In 1891 Cheret began to design posters without lettering to frame and hang on walls—still an unusual idea since prints were usually stored in portfolios. The explosion in color lithography was also encouraged by the use of zinc plates, which were lighter, cheaper, and more pliable than traditional lithographic stones. Also important was the formation of artist's organizations like the Société des artistes lithographie (Society of Lithographic Artists) and the Société de l'estampe originale (Society of Original Prints), which stimulated original printmaking. By the 1890s a proliferation of fine printers, independent exhibitions, publications devoted to prints, critics, publishers, and dealers like Sagot, all supported color lithography.

works.title: The Square at Evening
works.maker: Pierre Bonnard (French, 1867–1947), Published by Ambroise Vollard; Printed by Auguste Clot
works.credit: Some Scenes of Parisian Life: The Square at Evening, 1899. Pierre Bonnard (French, 1867–1947), Published by Ambroise Vollard; Printed by Auguste Clot. Lithograph; sheet: 40.3 x 53 cm (15 7/8 x 20 7/8 in.); image: 27 x 38 cm (10 5/8 x 14 15/16 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of the Hanna Fund, 1948.156.7
works.intro: By the mid-19th century lithography was used primarily for commercial purposes, but was revived as a creative artistic medium by the success of color printing. The growing popularity of posters by artists such as Jules Cheret (1836-1932) and Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec contributed to a renewed interest in color lithography at the end of the century. In addition, zinc plates, which are lighter, cheaper, and more flexible than traditional lithographic stones, had been perfected. There was also the influence of Japanese color woodblock prints and the formation of artist's organizations, like the Société des artistes lithographes Français (Society of French Lithographic Artists) and the Société de l'estampe originale (Society of the Original Print), to stimulate printmaking. By the 1890s a proliferation of fine printers, dealers, independent exhibitions, publications devoted to original prints, critics, and publishers all supported color lithography, which flourished in France as the favored printmaking medium of avant-garde artists.

works.title: Phänomen Vase
works.credit: Phänomen Vase, c. 1898–1903. Johann Lötz Witwe, Klostermühle (German). Glass; height: 25.4 cm (10 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of the family of Harold S. Meyer, 2024.102
works.intro: Johann Lötz Witwe was a renowned Bohemian glass manufacturer whose works are outstanding examples of Art Nouveau glass. In the 1890s, it produced cheaper versions of Tiffany’s colored glasses with metallic iridescence. Eventually, the Bohemian factory developed its own aesthetic and technique and commissioned leading designers of the Vienna Secession movement. The Phänomen (Phenomenon) range, patented in 1898, is one of the signature products of Lötz.

works.title: Strawberry Thief
works.credit: Strawberry Thief, c 1936. Designed by William Morris (British, 1834–1896). Plain weave cotton, discharge printed; overall: 88.3 x 99.1 cm (34 3/4 x 39 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mrs. Henry Chisholm, 1937.696
works.intro: Perhaps the most recognizable of Morris’s textiles, Strawberry Thief celebrates the thrushes in Kelmscott Manor’s garden. May Morris remarked, “You can picture my Father going out in the early morning and watching the rascally thrushes at work on the fruit beds and telling the gardener who growls, ‘I’d like to wring their necks!’ that no bird in the garden must be touched.” With Strawberry Thief, Morris perfected the indigo-discharge process, which required the entire cloth to be dyed blue before it was bleached and block printed, in this case with more colors than any of his other textiles.

works.title: Peacock and Dragon
works.credit: Peacock and Dragon , 1878. William Morris (British, 1834–1896). Weft-faced compound twill; wool; overall: 206.6 x 174.7 cm (81 5/16 x 68 3/4 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mrs. Philip White, 1953.330
works.intro: Morris sought to produce textiles that could function as he imagined medieval wall hangings had, bringing warmth to stone-cold rooms. Boldly designed with soothing colors in thick wool, Peacock and Dragon is the closest Morris came to achieving this ideal. In the same year he designed this textile, Morris visited the shop of the London dealer Vincent Robinson, where he saw a room re-created from Damascus, “all vermillion and gold and ultramarine, very beautiful, and is just like going into the Arabian nights.” It partly inspired the exotic motifs seen here. This design was one of the most popular among Morris’s customers; it was available in five colorways.

works.title: Jack-in-the-Pulpit Vase
works.maker: Quezal Art Glass and Decorating Company (American, 1901–1924)
works.credit: Jack-in-the-Pulpit Vase, c. 1900–1920. Quezal Art Glass and Decorating Company (American, 1901–1924). Blown glass; 30.5 x 20.3 cm (12 x 8 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of June Greenwald, 2019.244
works.intro: The Quezal Art Glass and Decorating Company was begun by former employees of Louis Comfort Tiffany as a rival operation in 1902. With its expressive form and brilliant golden iridescence, this vase represents the finest work produced by the Queens, New York, company in the Art Nouveau style.

works.title: Interior with Pink Wallpaper III
works.credit: Landscapes and Interiors: Interior with Pink Wallpaper III, 1899. Édouard Vuillard (French, 1868–1940). Color lithograph; sheet: 39.2 x 34 cm (15 7/16 x 13 3/8 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of the Hanna Fund, 1951.65.8
works.intro: The optical beauty of the patterning and luscious color of Interior with Wallpaper I, II, and III distracts from their ambivalent undercurrents. Across the three sheets, Vuillard creates an airless enclosure in which the wallpaper replicates itself, metastasizing across the surface and threatening the figures partially glimpsed through interior doors. Hidden figures recur in Vuillard’s work, adding an element of the uncanny to familiar settings.

works.title: Cabinet
works.medium: wood with metal inlays and painted parchment, glass doors and mirror
works.credit: Cabinet, c. 1895. Carlo Bugatti (Italian, 1856–1940). Wood with metal inlays and painted parchment, glass doors and mirror; overall: 224.5 x 141 x 55.3 cm (88 3/8 x 55 1/2 x 21 3/4 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Barry Friedman and Patricia Pastor, New York, 1984.177
works.intro: In both form and decoration this cabinet typifies the work of Carlo Bugatti. Asymmetrical, with a tower-like element at one side, there are Islamic-inspired ornaments throughout its design, notably the onion-shaped arches in the upper half of the cabinet. Japanese influence is also evident in the white metal inlays and in the sepia-painted parchment panels. The cabinet displays an extensive vocabulary of other decorative devices, including the partial ebonized frame, the turned wooden ornaments, metal reliefs, mirrored and green glass, and silk tassels. Despite their diversity, Bugatti organized all these elements into a coherent design.

works.title: Tea Table
works.medium: inlaid wood (mahogany?), cast and gilded bronze mounts, inlays of ivory or bone, metal, and mother-of-pearl (marine mussels or pearl oysters)
works.credit: Tea Table, c. 1907. Carlo Bugatti (Italian, 1856–1940). Inlaid wood (mahogany?), cast and gilded bronze mounts, inlays of ivory or bone, metal, and mother-of-pearl (marine mussels or pearl oysters); overall: 71.5 x 67.1 x 41.3 cm (28 1/8 x 26 7/16 x 16 1/4 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Leonard C. Hanna Jr. Fund, 1991.45
works.intro: Luxurious materials might catch the eye first, but a closer look reveals the imaginary creatures that adorn the surface of this table. Featuring elaborate arches, a favorite motif that appeared throughout Bugatti's furniture, this fantastical imagery is a window into the designer's expressive imagination.

works.title: Bench
works.credit: Bench, c. 1900. Attributed to Louis Majorelle (French, 1859–1926). Gilt wood; overall: 75 x 118.1 x 40.7 cm (29 1/2 x 46 1/2 x 16 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, James Parmelee Fund, 1971.28
works.intro: In the 20th century, designers of French furniture in the Art Nouveau style began to take inspiration from Rococo pieces of around 1750. With its gently curving forms, this bench exhibits the Majorelle firm's version of this refined taste. It is presently covered with a Japanese brocade of about 1900.

works.title: Cabinet
works.credit: Cabinet, c. 1910. Louis Majorelle (French, 1859–1926). Wood marquetry with metal mounts; overall: 130.8 x 162.5 x 58.4 cm (51 1/2 x 64 x 23 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, John L. Severance Fund, 1976.53
works.intro: The Majorelle family operated a large furniture making business at Nancy in eastern France. There they produced distinguished furniture in the Art Nouveau style. That style is well illustrated in the curvilinear, abstract wood marquetry (an inlaid, veneered pattern) on the doors of this cabinet.
